item.title: FAA ground stop still affecting thousands of flights. And, Trump meets Xi, Putin in Asia
item.description: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that things could be back to normal at the end of Monday after an FAA ground stop disrupted flights. And, Trump heads to Asia for a high-profile trilateral summit.

item.title: These birds fly 17,000 miles every year. Climate change could make it harder
item.description: Migratory birds cross the entire globe, carefully timing their journeys with the seasons. In a hotter climate, that timing is increasingly out of sync.

item.title: NPR's Student Podcast Challenge is back for 2027
item.description: The annual audio competition for grades four through 12 returns in January. Now in its ninth year, the contest has involved more than 90,000 students around the country.

item.title: Why sleep matters when it comes to weight gain and loss
item.description: Sleep can have a powerful impact on weight. Research shows it can affect appetite. There is also a two-way relationship between sleep quality and diet.

item.title: They saw people losing food benefits. So they started handing out free groceries
item.description: The cuts and changes to SNAP have been difficult for government workers who take pride in helping others. In San Diego, workers said they couldn't sit back while their neighbors went hungry.
